title: Deviation from linear reduced dynamics always occurs for each non-factorisable system-environment unitary evolution
abstract: In the simplest approximation, the reduced dynamics of a quantum system $S$ interacting with its environment $E$ is considered to be given by a completely positive map. But, in general, this is not the case. In fact, the reduced dynamics of the system in not even linear, in general. Whether the reduced dynamics is linear or not is determined by two factors: the set of possible initial states of the system-environment $\mathcal{S}=\left\lbrace ρ_{SE} \right\rbrace $, and the joint system-environment unitary evolution $U$. When $U$ is factorisable as $U=U_S\otimes U_E$, then we can choose $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{D}$, where $\mathcal{D}$ is the set of all system-environment density operators. In other words, when $U$ is factorisable, the reduced dynamics of the system $S$ is linear (in fact unitary) for arbitrary initial state of the system-environment $ρ_{SE}$. We show that this result cannot be generalized to any non-factorisable $U$: For any non-factorisable unitary evolution of the whole system-environment $U$, the set $\mathcal{S}$ must be chosen as a proper subset of $\mathcal{D}$ to achieve linear reduced dynamics. As a byproduct, considering a convex set of possible initial states of the system-environment $\mathcal{S}$ such that $\mathrm{Tr}_{E} \ \mathcal{S}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E} \ \mathcal{D}$, we show that when the reduced dynamics of the system, for one system-environment unitary evolution $U_1$, is positive, but not completely positive, this implies that reduced dynamics is not linear for another $U_2$.
summary: This theoretical paper rigorously analyzes when the reduced dynamics of a quantum system coupled to an environment remains linear. It proves that linearity requires the total system-environment unitary evolution to be factorisable. Crucially, it demonstrates that any non-factorisable evolution necessarily leads to a deviation from simple linear or completely positive dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which the reduced dynamics of a quantum system interacting with an environment remains linear, particularly when the total system-environment unitary evolution is non-factorisable.
main_result: The reduced dynamics is linear for arbitrary initial states if and only if the total unitary evolution $U$ is factorisable ($U=U_S \otimes U_E$). Furthermore, non-factorisable evolution implies deviations from linearity or complete positivity.
method: The analysis uses the mathematical framework of reduced density operators ($	ext{Tr}_E \circ 	ext{Ad}_U(ho_{SE})$) and compares the dynamics derived from different assumptions (e.g., CP maps vs. general linear maps) to deduce constraints on the unitary $U$.
model_or_system: The system consists of a quantum system $S$ coupled to an environment $E$, evolving unitarily under $U$. The dynamics are studied by analyzing the reduced density matrix $ho_S = 	ext{Tr}_E(ho_{SE})$.
key_observables: Reduced dynamics ($ho'_S$), deviation from complete positivity (CP), and linearity of the reduced map.
important_parameters: The structure of the initial state set $\mathcal{S}$ relative to the full set $\mathcal{D}$, and the factorisability of the unitary $U$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often starts by considering the simplest approximation (CP map) and then generalizes to arbitrary initial states and unitaries to find where this approximation breaks down.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the necessary and sufficient condition for linear reduced dynamics (factorisability of $U$). It then uses this result to show that non-factorisable $U$ forces deviations from linearity or CP, culminating in proofs that demonstrate this deviation always occurs.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental mathematical constraints on the description of open quantum systems, showing that simple assumptions (like CP maps) fail when initial correlations are present and the total evolution is non-factorisable.
